finding.claim: Admin listener exposes unauthenticated KV PUT/DELETE/LIST (and /metrics, /ready verbose) with no authentication and no Host validation, so any reachable client (or a DNS-rebinding page against a loopback-bound admin port) can read and overwrite KV store entries.
finding.source: Any network client reaching admin_addr (precondition: admin listener reachable; bind address is configuration outside this tree). Host header is never checked.

trace.note: add_admin_endpoints_to_pingora_server binds PingoraAdminService on admin_addr
path starting with /api/kv/ dispatched with no auth check
resolve_kv_route maps PUT/DELETE/GET on path alone
handle_set writes value with no owner/role check
handle_delete removes key with no owner/role check

finding.guards_checked: Body cap 1 MiB (kv/mod.rs:129); capacity limit 507 (kv/mod.rs:173); UTF-8 validation; JSON escaping on output; exact route-shape matching. No authentication, authorization, or Host allowlist exists on this path.

finding.claim: Requests carrying both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding are not rejected; TE is stripped for the upstream while the client's CL is forwarded, which can desynchronise upstream request framing (request smuggling). Exploitability depends on Pingora's HTTP/1 parser, which is not in the tree.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied request headers: Content-Length: N together with Transfer-Encoding: chunked
finding.sink: Upstream request framing (forwarded headers and body)

trace.note: SINGLE_VALUE_HEADERS covers only Content-Length and Content-Type; no CL vs TE comparison
normalize_request_headers runs; no CL+TE rejection
strip_hop_by_hop removes transfer-encoding (hop_by_hop.rs:31) but keeps content-length
apply_mutated_content_length rewrites CL only when a body writer mutated the body; unmutated bodies keep client CL

finding.guards_checked: Conflicting duplicate CL/Content-Type rejection; obs-fold rejection on Host and Content-Length; hop-by-hop stripping; StreamBuffer CL rewrite on mutation only. No CL+TE conflict check. Pingora parser behaviour unverified.

finding.claim: Max-Forwards: 0 on OPTIONS or TRACE is answered directly before the filter pipeline runs, bypassing configured authentication, allow/deny, rate-limit, metrics, and response-filter stages.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled request: method OPTIONS or TRACE with Max-Forwards: 0
finding.sink: Direct response (200 or TRACE echo) that skips the filter pipeline and response filters

trace.note: handle_max_forwards runs before run_pipeline (line 133)
mf == 0 short-circuit
send_rejection writes response directly, skipping response filters

finding.guards_checked: Method restricted to TRACE and OPTIONS; TRACE echo limited to allowlisted headers with Authorization/Cookie redacted (stream_buffer.rs:26-38); no upstream data returned.

finding.claim: In StreamBuffer mode, body-phase filters execute and buffer up to max_bytes before header-phase filters run, so header-phase deny decisions are applied after body filters have already executed for unauthenticated requests.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated client sending a body to a StreamBuffer route
finding.sink: Body filter execution and buffering before the header-phase pipeline's deny decision

trace.note: pre_read_body invoked when body mode is StreamBuffer
execute_http_request_body runs per chunk before headers pipeline
run_pipeline (header phase) only after pre-read completes
execute_http_request runs header filters after body filters

finding.guards_checked: max_bytes cap with ABSOLUTE_MAX_BODY_BYTES fallback; 413 on overflow (stream_buffer.rs:147-151). Which body filters exist and whether they have side effects is in praxis_filter, not verified.

finding.claim: A body-phase TerminalResponse decision is discarded and treated as Continue, so the body is forwarded upstream. This is consistent with the non-pre-read path (request_body_filter.rs:103) and is a fail-open only if praxis_filter defines TerminalResponse as a valid body-phase deny.
finding.source: A body filter returning FilterAction::TerminalResponse (for example a policy denial)
finding.sink: Upstream forwarding of the request body

trace.note: TerminalResponse matched to {} (Continue)
same mapping in the non-pre-read body path

finding.guards_checked: Reject and Err outcomes are handled (stream_buffer.rs:221-224). TerminalResponse semantics in praxis_filter not verified.

finding.claim: SSRF private-address guard relies on praxis_core::is_private_ip, and the unit tests do not cover unspecified addresses (0.0.0.0, ::). If is_private_ip does not flag them, an attacker-influenced upstream mapping could reach localhost services.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled SNI routed by an out-of-tree filter to an upstream address (precondition; not reachable from the in-tree static upstream path)

trace.note: SNI peeked from attacker ClientHello when no static upstream
run_connect_filters selects upstream_addr
lookup_host resolves upstream_addr
find_private_addr check unless allow_private_upstreams
connect to the same resolved addresses (no rebinding window)

finding.guards_checked: Resolve-then-check-then-connect to same addresses (prevents DNS rebinding); private check over all resolved IPs; connect timeout 10 s; SNI peek timeout 5 s and PEEK_MAX 16 KiB; global and per-listener connection caps. Coverage of 0.0.0.0 and :: in praxis_core::is_private_ip not verified.
